headline: ChatGPT wins as the best paid AI assistant on Android after extensive testing
summary: An analyst replaced Gemini with Claude, ChatGPT, and Copilot on Android to find the best daily workflow assistant. One proved superior for paid use.
details: The author questioned if Gemini was truly the best AI on Android or just the most convenient default option. They decided to test Claude, ChatGPT, and Copilot to see which offered the most value for daily use and was worth paying for.

Copilot offered a largely positive experience, especially for Microsoft ecosystem users, handling quick answers and basic writing well. However, its image generation was slow, and the app situation was confusing with a separate Microsoft 365 Copilot.

A major drawback for Copilot was the absence of Notebooks on mobile, a feature useful for ongoing projects on desktop. This made the mobile experience feel incomplete, positioning it more as a helpful add-on than a primary paid AI assistant.

Claude's Android app was clean, fast, and excellent at understanding messy prompts, rewriting text, and summarizing long information. Features like Code and Projects were highly useful for organizing related context.

Despite its strengths, Claude missed two key features: image generation for social media and scheduled tasks or actions. These omissions prevented it from becoming the author's preferred daily paid assistant on Android.

ChatGPT emerged as the clear winner due to its polished, fast, and predictable app experience. Its answers were consistently sharp, useful, and human-like, often requiring less rewriting than responses from Gemini or Copilot.

ChatGPT's feature set, including Projects for organizing chats, files, and context, felt more complete for daily use. Thanks to recent updates, the ability to set up recurring tasks further enhanced its utility and solidified its position as the top choice.

headline_marked: [[Steam Machine scalping hits $3,000]] on eBay, with pre-order reservations selling for 2X MSRP
headline: Steam Machine scalping hits $3,000 on eBay, with pre-order reservations selling for 2X MSRP
summary: Scalpers are selling Steam Machine pre-order slots on eBay for up to $2,899, more than double the retail price for the 2TB model. Valve's efforts to prevent this have not entirely stopped opportunists.
details: Steam Machine pre-order slots are being resold on eBay for significant premiums. The 512GB version is listed between $1,363.70 and $2,800, a 30% to 167% markup. The 2TB model sees even higher prices, ranging from $2,399 to $2,899, making it 93% to 140% more expensive than its $1,049 retail price.

Valve anticipated this scalping due to high demand and limited supply, a common issue seen with PlayStation 5 and Nvidia GPUs. To combat this, they implemented a randomized reservation system. This system aims to make purchases fairer for legitimate gamers by removing the rush of a specific launch time.

The reservation system accepts sign-ups over several days, allowing for validation of accounts and limiting one Steam Machine per household. Strict requirements include a Steam account in good standing and a prior Steam purchase by April 27, 2026. These measures are designed to deter professional scalpers.

Despite Valve's precautions, some individuals are still listing their reservation slots for sale. Buyers are strongly advised against purchasing from scalpers due to risks like potential scams, even from sellers with high ratings. There's no guarantee the seller is legitimate or that the item will be shipped after payment.

Waiting might be a better option, as the first batch of Steam Machines will only feature a single 16GB RAM stick, lacking dual-channel memory benefits. Valve has indicated that future releases might incorporate two 8GB sticks, potentially offering improved performance.
